steps.title: Vouvray
steps.body: Vouvray, near Tours, grows Chenin on tuffeau limestone and flint-clay, perruches, above the Loire. It makes every style, from sparkling to sweet. Vineyards with aubuis, clay-limestone, give rich wines. Producers like Huet, biodynamic since 1990, made it famous. Montlouis, across the river, is similar but often slightly lighter.

steps.title: Savennières
steps.body: Savennières, west of Angers, on schist and volcanic rock, is famous for dry Chenin: powerful, austere, mineral and long-lived. It has two famous crus: La Coulée de Serrant, a monopole of Nicolas Joly, a biodynamic pioneer, and La Roche aux Moines. Young Savennières can be closed; it needs 10 years to open.

steps.prompt: Match each term to its Loire meaning.
steps.explanation: Each appellation has its own soils and names.

steps.body: Decant a young Savennières. Like a red wine, it opens with air, revealing quince, honey and chamomile.

steps.prompt: Savennières is best known for sweet wines.
steps.explanation: Not true. Savennières is famous for powerful, dry Chenin.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Vouvray makes every style on tuffeau and flint
Savennières makes powerful, dry Chenin on schist
Coulée de Serrant is a famous biodynamic monopole
